_readme: These Kimi Code values cross the Go and TypeScript boundary. LeapMux runs kimi web and drives its kap-server through REST and one WebSocket. Native subscriptions deliver the latest turn page and subsequent turn and item changes for each selected agent. Older turn pages come from REST. The acknowledgement precedes initial state, so input admission waits for a complete conversation snapshot. Child subscriptions include their exact native agent IDs. The Worker stores immutable conversation records with native session, agent, turn and item ownership. The optional step index is metadata. Scoped conversation supplements carry authoritative revisions while preserving the original records. Native tool items retain their name and input alongside their result. Native task outcomes remain separate from child activity. Flat agent, usage, goal, todo, task and task.list frames carry unsequenced state. Native interaction frames carry approvals and questions with nested requests. Control replies use the unified interaction route. Subscription notices and recoverable conversation failures retain their native diagnostic fields and ownership. Each delivery has its own Worker receipt because the native feed supplies no notice event ID. A recoverable conversation failure cancels older history work and holds admission until a replacement snapshot arrives. The browser reads native output headers and file pointers while preserving the preview. An explicit native tool output remains authoritative, including an empty string. The Worker fetches session media through the authenticated API and checks its media type and digest. The browser resolves scoped supplements into a display copy. Original native item fields remain intact. The native read-only configuration validator recovers startup warnings emitted before subscription. The Worker removes repeated global configuration warnings. Moonshot AI owns native values. LeapMux owns the plan value of its permission axis and permission_mode in a plan-approval reply, which selects the native permission mode after approval. Native turn outcomes and end reasons determine completion and interruption. Native public user origins retain their specific skill, plugin, scheduler and hook fields. Model-tool skill activation exposes its public request and result; private activation metadata remains with the engine. The shared tables cover vocabulary LeapMux interprets. Each unread field states which side retains its bytes without interpreting them.

KimiApprovalReply.doc:
KimiApprovalReply is the body that answers one approval, as the worker stores it.

The worker posts it to `/sessions/{id}/interactions/{interaction_id}` without
`permission_mode`, which is LeapMux's own: it states the mode an approved plan
or goal start switches to, and the worker applies it before it posts the
decision.

KimiQuestionReply.doc:
KimiQuestionReply answers one native question through the interaction route.
The body contains exactly one of Answers or Dismissed, with Kind set to question.

KimiDecisionFields.doc:
KimiDecisionFields are the fields that AnswerControlRequest writes beside the
neutral `behavior` of its answer: the approval scope, and a question's answers
in the server's own shape.

KimiConversationRecord.doc:
KimiConversationRecord is an immutable Worker view of one native conversation item, turn or notice.
It keeps native identities and public fields without pretending to be an upstream packet.
Later authoritative views enrich the same stored record through conversationSupplement.

KimiConversationMediaFile.doc: KimiConversationMediaFile retains verified bytes recovered from the owned native media route.

KimiConversationMediaReceipt.doc: KimiConversationMediaReceipt binds recovered image bytes to one native tool item. It is rendering data, separate from authoritative conversation revisions.

KimiConversationTurnContext.doc: KimiConversationTurnContext binds an item view to its native turn without copying growing step or usage data. Tool requests never carry outcome context.

KimiConversationFailure.doc: KimiConversationFailure retains the native identity and diagnostic fields of turns.failed. It describes a conversation subscription failure, not a model turn outcome.
